newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but off highs.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm but off highs.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended the week with strong gains following overnight comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that Japan was overly pessimistic about its economy.
"Greenspan's comment triggered the market to reverse all the way up. The financial stocks recovered and there was some arbitrage-related buying on the index as well," said a Japanese bank dealer.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended 420 points higher at 18,320 after touching a peak at 18,625.
"The potential to break higher is there. But at the same time, I won't be surprised if it drifts down," said the dealer.
He said the slew of comments by Japanese officials about stock prices, forex movements and the state of the economy had left the market largely unimpressed.
"They're saying the economy's not in danger. But on the other hand, it's not really improving either," he said.
A trader with a local institution said the March Nikkei's failure to reach the key technical level of 18,750 had prompted some long liquidations before the close.
"The medium-term trend is still sideways to down, rather than up," he said, adding that it needed to close above 18,750 to head higher. On the downside, support is seen around 17,300.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended 2.5 points above its opening 312.0 on volume of 310 lots.
